data: Classical Physics: Energy and Force II

We explore the applications of the laws of classical mechanics to a variety of dynamical systems, such as the motion of fluids (which allows for the flight of airplanes), the orbits of planets and other celestial bodies under the influence of gravity, and the movement of bodies in non-inertial frames (such as winds and ocean currents on the rotating earth). These form the basis for more advanced fields such as astronomy and climate science. Deeper questions about motion in inertial and non-inertial frames lead naturally to Einstein’s general theory of relativity.We explore the applications of the laws of classical mechanics to a variety of dynamical systems, such as the motion of fluids (which allows for the flight of airplanes), the orbits of planets and other celestial bodies under the influence of gravity, and the movement of bodies in non-inertial frames (such as winds and ocean currents on the rotating earth).
